arxiv-1903-00715.title: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for StarCraft by Abstract Forward Models and Transfer Learning
arxiv-1903-00715.creator: Ruo-Ze Liu, Haifeng Guo, Xiaozhong Ji, Yang Yu, Zhen-Jia Pang, Zitai Xiao, Yuzhou Wu, Tong Lu
arxiv-1903-00715.description: Abstract Injecting human knowledge is an effective way to accelerate reinforcement learning (RL). However, these methods are underexplored. This paper presents our discovery that an abstract forward model (Thought-game (TG)) combined with transfer learning is an effective way. We take StarCraft II as the study environment.

arxiv-1910-10822.title: Wasserstein total variation filtering
arxiv-1910-10822.creator: Erdem Varol, Amin Nejatbakhsh
arxiv-1910-10822.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Erdem Varol, Amin Nejatbakhsh. In this paper, we expand upon the theory of trend filtering by introducing the use of the Wasserstein metric as a means to control the amount of spatiotemporal variation in filtered time series data. While trend filtering utilizes regularization to produce signal estimates that are piecewise linear, in the case of ℓ 1 \ell_{1} regularization, or temporally smooth, in the case of ℓ 2 \ell_{2} regularization, it ignores the topology of the spatial distribution of signal.

arxiv-2103-02569.title: Higgs-like spectator field as the origin of structure
arxiv-2103-02569.creator: Alexandros Karam, Tommi Markkanen, Luca Marzola, Sami Nurmi, Martti Raidal, Arttu Rajantie
arxiv-2103-02569.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alexandros Karam, Tommi Markkanen, Luca Marzola, Sami Nurmi, Martti Raidal, Arttu Rajantie. We show that the observed primordial perturbations can be entirely sourced by a light spectator scalar field with a quartic potential, akin to the Higgs boson, provided that the field is sufficiently displaced from vacuum during inflation. The framework relies on the indirect modulation of reheating, which is implemented without any direct coupling between the spectator field and the inflaton and does not require non-renormalisable interactions.

arxiv-2110-00938.title: Search for α \alpha condensed states in 13 C using α \alpha inelastic scattering
arxiv-2110-00938.creator: K. Inaba, Y. Sasamoto, T. Kawabata, M. Fujiwara, Y. Funaki, K. Hatanaka, K. Itoh, M. Itoh, K. Kawase, H. Matsubara, Y. Maeda, K. Suda, S. Sakaguchi, Y. Shimizu, A. Tamii, Y. Tameshige, M. Uchida, T. Uesaka, T. Yamada, H. P. Yoshida
arxiv-2110-00938.description: Abstract We searched for the α \alpha condensed state in 13 C by measuring the α \alpha inelastic scattering at E α = 388 E_{\alpha}=388 MeV at forward angles including 0 degrees. We performed the distorted-wave Born-approximation calculation with the single-folding potential and the multipole decomposition analysis to determine the isoscalar transition strengths in 13 C.

arxiv-2210-16116.title: Adiabatic processes like isothermal processes
arxiv-2210-16116.creator: Pierre Nazé
arxiv-2210-16116.description: Abstract The objective of this work is to show that adiabatic processes can be very similar to isothermal ones. First, we show that the criteria for the compatibility of linear-response theory with the Second Law of Thermodynamics for thermally isolated systems are the same as those for systems performing isothermal processes.

arxiv-2308-01248.title: A hybrid approach to Real-Time Multi-Target Tracking
arxiv-2308-01248.creator: VM Scarrica, C Panariello, A Ferone, A Staiano
arxiv-2308-01248.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by VM Scarrica, C Panariello, A Ferone, A Staiano. Multi-Object Tracking, also known as Multi-Target Tracking, is a significant area of computer vision that has many uses in a variety of settings. The development of deep learning, which has encouraged researchers to propose more and more work in this direction, has significantly impacted the scientific advancement around the study of tracking as well as many other domains related to computer vision.

arxiv-2308-06674.title: Nonadiabatic holonomic quantum computation based on commutation relation
arxiv-2308-06674.creator: P. Z. Zhao, D. M. Tong
arxiv-2308-06674.description: Abstract Nonadiabatic holonomic quantum computation has received increasing attention due to the merits of both robustness against control errors and high-speed implementation. A crucial step in realizing nonadiabatic holonomic quantum computation is to remove the dynamical phase from the total phase. arxiv-2309-17273.title: Characterizing losses in InAs two-dimensional electron gas-based gatemon qubits
arxiv-2309-17273.creator: William M. Strickland 1, Lukas J. Baker 1, Jaewoo Lee 1, Krishna Dindial 1, Bassel Heiba Elfeky 1, Patrick J. Strohbeen 1, Mehdi Hatefipour 1, Peng Yu 1, Ido Levy 1, Jacob Issokson 1, Vladimir E. Manucharyan 2, Javad Shabani 1
arxiv-2309-17273.description: Abstract The tunnelling of cooper pairs across a Josephson junction (JJ) allow for the nonlinear inductance necessary to construct superconducting qubits, amplifiers, and various other quantum circuits. An alternative approach using hybrid superconductor-semiconductor JJs can enable superconducting qubit architectures with all electric control.

arxiv-2310-02923.title: A Unitary Operator Construction Solution Based on Pauli Group for Maximal Dense Coding
arxiv-2310-02923.creator: Wenjie Liu, Junxiu Chen, Wenbin Yu, Zhihao Liu, Hanwu Chen
arxiv-2310-02923.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wenjie Liu, Junxiu Chen, Wenbin Yu, Zhihao Liu, Hanwu Chen. Quantum dense coding plays an important role in quantum cryptography communication, and how to select a set of appropriate unitary operators to encode message is the primary work in the design of quantum communication protocols. proposed a preliminary method for unitary operator construction based on Pauli group under multiplication, which is used for dense coding in quantum dialogue.

arxiv-2403-18123.title: Planck data revisited: low-noise synchrotron polarisation maps from the WMAP and Planck space missions
arxiv-2403-18123.creator: Jacques Delabrouille
arxiv-2403-18123.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jacques Delabrouille. Observations of cosmic microwave background polarisation, essential for probing a potential phase of inflation in the early universe, suffer from contamination by polarised emission from the Galactic interstellar medium. This work combines existing observations from the WMAP and Planck space missions to make a low-noise map of polarised synchrotron emission that can be used to clean forthcoming CMB observations.

arxiv-2409-17418.title: Astrophysical systematics on testing general relativity with gravitational waves from galactic double white dwarfs
arxiv-2409-17418.creator: Shu Yan Lau, Kent Yagi, Phil Arras
arxiv-2409-17418.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shu Yan Lau, Kent Yagi, Phil Arras. Gravitational waves have been shown to provide new constraints on gravitational theories beyond general relativity (GR), especially in the strong field regime. Gravitational wave signals from galactic double white dwarfs, expected to be detected by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), also have the potential to place stringent bounds on certain theories that give rise to relatively large deviations from GR in less compact binaries, such as through scalar radiation.

arxiv-2510-03593.title: Mean Values at Hopf Points and Oscillation-Induced Gain Modulation
arxiv-2510-03593.creator: William Harold Nesse, Cooper John Hutchinson
arxiv-2510-03593.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by William Harold Nesse, Cooper John Hutchinson. We present a result concerning the mean value of orbits emerging from Hopf bifurcations. We then apply this result to identify a new phenomenon termed oscillation-induced gain modulation .

pmc-10555212.title: FRI151 Combined Maternal Hyperandrogenemia And Maternal Western Diet Consumption Programs Hypertension In Adult Female Offspring That Is Associated With Increased Leptin Levels
pmc-10555212.creator: Noha M Shawky, Ruth M Quin, Kacey Davenport
pmc-10555212.description: Disclosure: N.M. Shawky: None. R.M. Quin: None. K. Davenport: None. Funding: P20GM121334, AHA Career Development Award 938320 Background: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the major cause of hyperandrogenemia and the most common endocrinopathy in women of reproductive age. There is still a great controversy on whether daughters of PCOS women develop PCOS themselves.

pmc-10563653.title: Procedural outcome and follow-up of stylet-driven leads compared with lumenless leads for left bundle branch area pacing
pmc-10563653.creator: Aarthiga Sritharan, Nikola Kozhuharov, Nicolas Masson, Elise Bakelants, Valérian Valiton, Haran Burri
pmc-10563653.description: AimsLeft bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is most often delivered using lumenless leads (LLLs), but may also be performed using stylet-driven leads (SDLs). There are limited reports on the comparison of these tools, mainly limited to reports describing initial operator experience or without detailed procedural data.

pmc-11659933.title: Antibodies in breast milk: Pro‐bodies designed for healthy newborn development
pmc-11659933.creator: Valerie Verhasselt, Julie Tellier, Rita Carsetti, Burcu Tepekule
pmc-11659933.description: SummaryThis manuscript sheds light on the impact of maternal breast milk antibodies on infant health. Milk antibodies prepare and protect the newborn against environmental exposure, guide and regulate the offspring's immune system, and promote transgenerational adaptation of the immune system to its environment.

pmc-11710010.title: Molecular environment in Alzheimer’s disease brain revealed by the hybrid imaging analyses
pmc-11710010.creator: Tadayuki Ogawa, Shino Homma‐Takeda, Tomonari Umemura, Takafumi Hirata, Yuko Saito
pmc-11710010.description: BackgroundAlthough amyloid deposition in brain is one of the hallmark pathological features of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), the upstream events and its molecular environment in AD brain remain largely unknown. Recent advances in analytical methods such as mass spectrometry can provide the cutting‐edge tools to unveil the AD pathogenesis at molecular and atomic level.

pmc-12531982.title: Schwannoma of the colon presenting as a submucosal lesion: diagnostic challenge and surgical management
pmc-12531982.creator: Mohammad Al Yaseen, Ali Toffaha, Hamza A Abdul-Hafez, Mohamed Kurer, Mohamed Abunada, Mahmood Al-Dhaheri
pmc-12531982.description: Schwannomas are rare benign nerve-sheath tumours that uncommonly involve the gastrointestinal tract, with the colon and rectum among the least frequent sites. We report a 36-year-old man with a 2-year history of central colicky abdominal pain, alternating bowel habits (predominantly constipation), intermittent rectal bleeding and bloating.

pmc-12639253.title: HIPEC with cisplatin desensitization at the time of secondary debulking in a patient with a prior carboplatin hypersensitivity reaction
pmc-12639253.creator: Michelle Greenman, Yasmin Abozenah, Yifang Eva Pan, Elena S Ratner, Gary Altwerger
pmc-12639253.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Highlights•First reported case of hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) with platinum desensitization.•Intravenous desensitization is established, but no standardized protocol exists for desensitization in HIPEC therapy.•A modified stepwise cisplatin perfusion allowed safe HIPEC, offering a strategy for platinum allergy in recurrence.Keywords: Hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy, HIPEC, Recurrent ovarian cancer, Platinum therapy, Platinum hypersensitivity, Desensitization protocol, Secondary cytoreductive surgery

Introduction

Hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) has gained increasing adoption in gynecologic oncology over the past decade, driven by recent multicenter phase III randomized controlled trials.

pmc-13086384.title: Evaluation of debris and smear layer removal efficacy of different irrigating solutions using the C-RCC irrigation system: An in vitro SEM study
pmc-13086384.creator: Manisha Goyal, Arushi Agarwal, Ankita Roy, Deepti Jain, Ashutosh Shandilya, Sanjeev Kunhappan
pmc-13086384.description: Background:Conventional use of sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) and ethylenediaminetetraacetate (EDTA) for debris and smear layer removal may weaken dentin and prolong clinical procedures, prompting a search for safer, more efficient, and multifunctional irrigants. Thus, the present study aimed to evaluate debris and smear layer removal efficacy of different irrigating solutions using C-RCC irrigator.

pmc-13249897.title: CLPX acquires an iron-sulfur cluster to sustain mitochondrial proteostasis in cancer cells
pmc-13249897.creator: Chengquan Huang, Yixue Zhang, Han Gao, Yuxin Song, Shunchang Hu, Chaoyue Sun, Shiwen Duan, Dongxiao Ma, Xiumei Jiang, Gang Liu
pmc-13249897.description: Mitochondrial proteostasis-maintaining mechanisms are crucial for protecting cells from the toxicity of misfolded protein accumulation. Although excessive stress is known to inactivate these mechanisms and thereby induce mitophagy in cancer cells, the detailed molecular mechanisms coordinating these mitochondrial quality control processes remain unclear.

pmc-13254208.title: Human–AI collaboration for dysphagia rehabilitation from effectiveness to implementation complexity: a systematic review
pmc-13254208.creator: Wenwen Yang, Sufang Li, Yifei Du, Mengran Chen, Funa Yang, Fan Zhang, Ji Zhao, Yanqing Li, Xiaoxia Xu

pmc-13520167.title: A multi-systemic ethical dilemma model in hemodialysis patients: a qualitative study
pmc-13520167.creator: Huiqing Zhu, Anjie Zhao, Yixing Zhou, Farong Zhang, Yuxiu Jia
pmc-13520167.description: BackgroundIn hemodialysis, patients navigate ethical tensions arising from the intersection of clinical demands, personal values, and systemic constraints. While existing research has focused largely on clinician perspectives, limited attention has been paid to how patients themselves experience and interpret these ethical dilemmas.

pmc-13656563.title: Not all older adults are viewed alike: feeling thermometer ratings toward older-adult subgroups in Japan
pmc-13656563.creator: Yuho Shimizu
pmc-13656563.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThis study examined whether feeling thermometer ratings toward older adults vary across older-adult subgroups and how such ratings are positioned relative to other common prejudice targets. Using an online sample of 520 Japanese adults aged 18–64, we assessed feeling thermometer ratings (0 = coldest, 100 = warmest) for 14 targets: nursing-home, on-deathbed, handicapped, solitary, senile, on-welfare, and grumpy older adults, as well as immigrants and refugees, foreign tourists, sexual minorities, racial minorities, and persons with mental, physical, or intellectual disabilities.
